name: Kara_no_Kyoukai_14_Organizations
description: Canon-accurate database of organizations, families, educational institutions, and occult networks relevant to Kara no Kyoukai and Fate/stay night cross-interaction. Covers the Ryougi and Asagami clans, Reien Girls' Academy, Garan no Dou, the Clock Tower and Sealing Designation Enforcers, the Holy Church, the Four Demon Hunter Houses, mundane police/underworld networks, and rogue heretical magi.

0.content:
<Org_Ryougi_Clan>
[ORGANIZATIONAL TYPE & IDENTITY]
Ancient Aristocratic Clan / Former Demon Hunter House (退魔四家, Taima Yonke). An indigenous Japanese lineage of extraordinary prestige, historical demon-slaying pedigree, and extensive modern economic and territorial holdings centered on the outskirts of Mifune City.

[STRUCTURE & KEY FIGURES]
- The Patriarch: Shiki's father and current head of the Ryougi household. A stern, traditional man steeped in classical martial discipline and feudal dignity. He recognizes Shiki's supernatural aptitude and formally designated her as the successor.
- Kaname Ryougi: Shiki's elder brother. An outwardly competent, respectable young man adept at mundane business, finance, and social politics, but completely devoid of the spiritual aptitude or dual-mind disposition required to inherit the clan's true martial heritage. He was bypassed for headship, harboring quiet, complex resignation.
- Ryougi Shiki: The designated heir. Bearer of the awakened dual-mind lineage and hereditary sword techniques.
- Retainers & Servants: Traditional groundskeepers, kimono fitters, and discreet family retainers who maintain the secluded bamboo forest compound and manage family affairs.

[IDEOLOGY & METHODS]
- Survival Through Detachment: The clan operates on cold, generational pragmatism. They do not seek glory, public recognition, or thaumaturgical prestige; they seek the perpetuation of their bloodline and independence from outside interference.
- The Dual-Mind Breeding: Unlike Western magi who pass down Magic Crests, the Ryougi practiced specialized mental conditioning and bloodline selection to produce heirs capable of housing two distinct human personalities (Yin/Shiki and Yang/SHIKI). This allowed the heir to bear the psychic and moral burden of lethal combat without shattering their core sanity.
- Mastery of the Blade: Rejection of Western incantations in favor of supreme physical, conceptual, and instinctive swordsmanship passed down through ancient ancestral blades (such as the Kanesada).

[RESOURCES & REGIONAL INFLUENCE]
- Vast Traditional Wealth: Extensive real estate, commercial landholdings, and mountainous forestry surrounding Mifune City.
- Political & Underworld Insulation: Deep historical connections to regional political authorities and local yakuza syndicates, granting the family de facto legal autonomy. Police quietly avoid probing deeply into Ryougi affairs or properties unless absolutely forced.
- The Mountain Compound: A sprawling, fortified traditional Japanese estate hidden within a dense bamboo forest, protected by natural seclusion and ancient wards.

[RELATIONSHIP WITH THE SUPERNATURAL]
- Indigenous Demon Hunters: Historically tasked with exterminating non-human entities and demonic mixed-bloods. They view Western magecraft with indifference or quiet condescension, viewing Clock Tower magi as meddlesome foreigners obsessed with sterile academic theories.

[INTERNAL CONFLICTS & SECRECY]
- Sibling Succession Rift: The quiet domestic tension of Kaname being bypassed in favor of a younger sister. While there is no open civil war, the dynamic is strained by traditional expectations versus esoteric necessity.
- Shiki's Two-Year Coma: Her hospitalization from 1996 to 1998 threw the family succession into limbo, forcing the elders to prepare for Kaname's possible reinstatement before her sudden awakening.
- Shiki's Deliberate Distance: Shiki despises the stifling formality, expectations, and political maneuvering of the estate, choosing to live alone in a bare, concrete municipal apartment.

[INTER-INSTITUTIONAL RELATIONSHIPS]
- Historical alliance with the Asagami, Fujou, and Nanaya (now completely dormant).
- Strict non-engagement with the Mage's Association and Holy Church.
- Respectful oversight of local Mifune underworld syndicates.

[OUTSIDER KNOWLEDGE & PERCEPTION]
- Mundane Society: Viewed as untouchable, old-money Japanese nobility or an aristocratic family with shadowy yakuza connections.
- Western Magi: Almost entirely ignorant of the Ryougi clan's existence and inner techniques.

[ROLEPLAY CONSEQUENCES & SCENE DIRECTION]
- Shiki has unlimited financial independence and legal insulation through her family name, but she never uses clan authority as a crutch.
- Family retainers will occasionally appear to deliver kimonos, funds, or formal requests from her father, creating quiet, formal, and tense scenes contrasting her minimalist life with feudal grandeur.
</Org_Ryougi_Clan>

1.content:
<Org_Asagami_Family>
[ORGANIZATIONAL TYPE & IDENTITY]
Fallen Demon Hunter House / Commercial Corporate Family. Formerly one of the Four Demon Hunter Houses known as the 浅神 (Asagami, "Shallow God"), now assimilated into mundane corporate capitalism under the modernized surname 浅上 (Asagami, "Shallow Above").

[STRUCTURE & KEY FIGURES]
- The Stepfather: Current head of the household and president of Asagami Construction. A calculating, paranoid, and status-conscious businessman who married into the family, terrified of the supernatural bloodline he married into.
- Asagami Fujino: The tragic daughter and heiress. Born with the dormant, unsealed psychic ability to bend and distort physical space, which was violently suppressed during her childhood.
- Corporate Staff & Fixers: Mundane corporate executives, site foremen, and private attorneys managing municipal building contracts and shielding the company from scandal.

[IDEOLOGY & METHODS]
- Rejection of the Occult Through Domestic Suppression: Driven by mortal terror of their ancient psychic heritage, the modern Asagami family chose to extinguish their supernatural identity to survive as respectable, wealthy members of modern Japanese society.
- Medical & Physical Anesthesia: When Fujino began manifesting minor telekinetic anomalies as a child, her stepfather subjected her to severe physical abuse and chemical/sensory suppression, successfully deadening her sensory nervous system (inducing chemically induced analgesia (acquired sensory block)) to seal away her psychic channels.

[RESOURCES & REGIONAL INFLUENCE]
- Commercial Construction Power: Heavy machinery fleets, construction yards, and commercial real estate investments across Mifune City.
- Municipal Influence: Strong ties to city redevelopment planning boards, winning contracts for public infrastructure and commercial skyscrapers (including the ill-fated Fujou Building project, which became a financial disaster for the firm).

[RELATIONSHIP WITH THE SUPERNATURAL]
- Complete Repression: The family possesses no thaumaturgical foundations, grimoires, or Magic Circuits. Their supernatural heritage consists purely of innate biological psychic mutation (Channeling/Spatial Distortion), which they treat as a cancerous curse to be hidden from the world at all costs.

[INTERNAL CONFLICTS & SECRECY]
- Domestic Cruelty & Clinical Deception: Fujino was raised in an environment of cold, clinical isolation, treated by her stepfather not as a daughter, but as a dangerous freak that had to remain numb to be tolerable.
- Financial Stress: Failed civic investments and construction delays created mounting corporate desperation for the family patriarch in the late 1990s.

[INTER-INSTITUTIONAL RELATIONSHIPS]
- Historical ties to the Ryougi family have lapsed entirely; the modern Asagami operate purely as business competitors or distant neighbors.
- Zero formal contact with the Clock Tower or the Holy Church until Touko investigated the supernatural destruction of the Minato Bridge.

[OUTSIDER KNOWLEDGE & PERCEPTION]
- Mundane Public: Recognized as a standard, mid-to-high tier regional construction corporation.
- School & Society: Fujino was enrolled in Reien Girls' Academy to maintain an appearance of aristocratic refinement while keeping her far away from the family home.

[ROLEPLAY CONSEQUENCES & SCENE DIRECTION]
- The Asagami represent the tragedy of ancient mystery decaying into petty corporate cruelty.
- Scenes involving the Asagami family or their construction sites evoke sterile offices, dust-covered architectural blueprints, concrete dust, and the suffocating psychological weight of emotional abuse and denied identity.
</Org_Asagami_Family>

<Org_Reien_Girls_Academy>
[ORGANIZATIONAL TYPE & IDENTITY]
Private Catholic Boarding School for Young Women (Educational Institution). An ultra-prestigious, conservative, and insular Christian academy situated in the secluded forested mountains on the perimeter of Mifune City.

[STRUCTURE & KEY FIGURES]
- Board of Trustees & Mother Superior: Catholic nuns and senior educators who enforce rigorous doctrinal discipline, scholastic excellence, and strict behavioral modesty.
- The Faculty: Conservative academic teachers, domestic science instructors, and visiting lecturers (including the sinister Kurogiri Satsuki, who infiltrated the academy as an English/ethics teacher using God's Word).
- The Student Body: Daughters of high-society families, politicians, corporate magnates, and ancient clans. Key students:
  - Kokutou Azaka: Top-tier honors student, Touko's secret apprentice, skilled in ignition magecraft.
  - Asagami Fujino: Placed here by her stepfather to maintain family prestige while remaining isolated.
  - Tachibana Kaori: Tragic student whose mysterious death became central to the school's occult crisis.

[IDEOLOGY & METHODS]
- Catholic Sanctity & Isolation: The academy operates on strict Christian principles of purity, humility, academic diligence, and total isolation from secular worldly corruption.
- Regimented Lifestyle: Students live year-round in gated campus dormitories, subject to strict curfews, mandatory morning and evening chapel services, uniform dress codes, and heavily monitored correspondence. Leaving campus requires rare parental authorizations.

[RESOURCES & CAMPUS GROUNDS]
- Pristine Gothic Architecture: A vast, private forested estate featuring Neo-Gothic brick dormitories, a towering chapel with stained glass, manicured courtyards, an expansive library, and iron perimeter gates locked every evening at sunset.
- Wealthy Endowment: Heavily subsidized by tuition from Japan's elite and international Catholic educational foundations, granting it state-of-the-art facilities hidden in serene mountain solitude.

[RELATIONSHIP WITH THE SUPERNATURAL]
- Mundane Facade & Occult Incubation: The school administration is 100% mundane and devoutly oblivious to real magecraft. However, the school's intense emotional atmosphere of adolescent repression, unspoken yearnings, and extreme isolation makes it a fragile petri dish for psychological and supernatural anomalies.
- Secret Magecraft Practice: Azaka secretly studies Touko's thaumaturgical texts and practices ignition spells inside her private dormitory room under the guise of late-night study sessions.

[INTERNAL CONFLICTS & SECRECY]
- Repression & Whispered Scandals: Beneath the pristine, hymn-singing facade lies intense adolescent social tension: covert romantic rivalries, strict hierarchical cliques, and whispered rumors of occultism or suicides quickly buried by the nuns to preserve the academy's immaculate reputation.
- The Kurogiri Incident: Kurogiri Satsuki utilized the school's secluded vulnerability to subject students to linguistic memory alteration and existential dread without outside interference.

[INTER-INSTITUTIONAL RELATIONSHIPS]
- Subordinate to the regional Catholic diocese, but strictly educational—completely detached from the militant Eighth Sacrament or Church Executors.
- Trusted by elite families (Kokutou, Asagami) as a secure sanctuary for young daughters.
- Unauthorized male visitors (including Mikiya or Clock Tower magi) are strictly forbidden from setting foot on campus.

[OUTSIDER KNOWLEDGE & PERCEPTION]
- Known across the prefecture as the pinnacle of elite female education—an untouchable, aristocratic finishing school producing refined, modest young ladies.

[ROLEPLAY CONSEQUENCES & SCENE DIRECTION]
- Scenes set at Reien must emphasize the suffocating quiet: ticking pendulum clocks, rustling pleated skirts on polished hardwood floors, the distant tolling of chapel bells, strict curfew patrols by nuns, and the tension of sneaking forbidden research or weapons through the locked iron gates.
</Org_Reien_Girls_Academy>

3.content:
<Org_Garan_no_Dou>
[ORGANIZATIONAL TYPE & IDENTITY]
Informal Occult Atelier / Independent Investigation Office & Architecture Studio (Workplace & Haven). A boutique architectural design, antiquities restoration, and puppet-crafting studio located on the top floor of a hollow, unfinished commercial concrete building in Mifune City. Functions as Aozaki Touko's private thaumaturgical workshop, research sanctuary, and base of operations.

[STRUCTURE & KEY PERSONNEL]
- Aozaki Touko: Sole proprietor, master magus, and Grand-rank puppeteer. Handles high-end architectural commissions, artisan doll restorations, thaumaturgical research, and covert supernatural crisis management.
- Kokutou Mikiya: Sole salaried employee. Functions as office manager, investigative researcher, mundane client liaison, and chief tea/coffee brewer. His extraordinary investigative talent provides the firm with deep civilian intelligence.
- Ryougi Shiki: Freelance associate and frequent visitor. Operates as Touko's primary combat operative when physical intervention or supernatural extermination is required, in exchange for Touko's prosthetic maintenance and occult insight.

[IDEOLOGY & METHODS]
- Pragmatic Independence: Touko operates outside the dogma of both the Clock Tower and the Church. She takes genuine architectural and restoration jobs to finance her extravagant tastes, while accepting supernatural contracts that either pique her intellectual curiosity or threaten her quiet exile.
- Division of Labor: Mikiya conducts exhaustive, ethical civilian detective work through public records and police contacts; Touko analyzes the metaphysical and thaumaturgical architecture; Shiki provides clean, lethal execution when diplomacy fails.

[RESOURCES & WORKSHOP ASSETS]
- Thaumaturgical Sanctuary: Multi-layered boundary fields (anti-scrying, intrusion detection, cognitive masking) that render the building invisible to casual passersby and hostile divination.
- Occult Storage: Locked basement and backroom crates housing spare biological puppet bodies, enchanted replacement prosthetics, rare alchemical ingredients, and antique thaumaturgical tomes.
- Mundane Comforts: High-end drafting tables, a lavish designer sofa, expensive smoking supplies, and an imported, professional-grade Italian espresso machine.

[RELATIONSHIP WITH THE SUPERNATURAL]
- An Unsanctioned Rogue Node: Touko is an unaligned magus operating under an active Clock Tower Sealing Designation. She refuses obedience to the local leylines, avoids the Church, and treats the entire city as her personal neutral territory.

[INTERNAL CONFLICTS & SECRECY]
- The Looming Threat of Enforcers: Touko must always be prepared to abandon the premises or destroy her records if Clock Tower pursuit agents locate her workshop.
- Ethical Friction: Mikiya's unwavering civilian moral compass frequently clashes with Touko's cold, detached magus pragmatism, forcing Touko to handle the darker aspects of occult contracts behind his back.
- Shiki's Aloof Presence: Shiki visits primarily to see Mikiya or repair her arm, treating Touko with sarcastic disrespect while lounging on the studio couch eating Häagen-Dazs.

[INTER-INSTITUTIONAL RELATIONSHIPS]
- Zero formal alliances. Maintains informal, indirect access to police files through Mikiya's cousin Daisuke Akimi. Actively conceals its presence from Clock Tower investigators and Fuyuki magi.

[OUTSIDER KNOWLEDGE & PERCEPTION]
- Mundane Clients: View Garan no Dou as an eccentric, ultra-exclusive boutique design atelier whose brilliant female architect works erratic hours surrounded by uncannily realistic mannequins.
- Law Enforcement: The police know Mikiya works there at a quiet design office; they have no suspicion of its supernatural function.

[ROLEPLAY CONSEQUENCES & SCENE DIRECTION]
- The primary safehouse, briefing hub, and philosophical decompression chamber.
- Scenes here feature the smell of freshly brewed dark roast coffee, drifting cigarette smoke, soft jazz on a radio, blueprints pinned to corkboards, and the eerie, glassy stares of lifeless puppet torsos resting in display cabinets.
</Org_Garan_no_Dou>

4.content:
<Org_Clock_Tower_Mages_Association>
[ORGANIZATIONAL TYPE & IDENTITY]
International Thaumaturgical Governance & Academic Oligarchy (Formal Organization). The supreme governing, academic, and political body of Western Magecraft, operating from the subterranean labyrinth beneath the British Museum in London.

[STRUCTURE & RELEVANT DEPARTMENTS]
- The Lords (君主, Lord): Twelve noble aristocratic lineages (such as Barthomeloi, Trambelio, Animusphere, and El-Melloi) who monopolize political power and chair the twelve primary faculties of thaumaturgical study.
- Relevant Faculties:
  - Department of Creation / Puppetry: The division where Aozaki Touko studied and achieved Grand (冠位) rank before her exile.
  - Sorgan School / Curse Arts: The pedantic, status-obsessed department associated with Cornelius Alba.
  - Faculty of Lore (Policies): Oversees the preservation of ancient mystery and enforces Association law.
- Field Enforcers & Bureaucrats: A sprawling network of administrative clerks, researchers, and armed combat agents deployed globally.

[IDEOLOGY & METHODS]
- Preservation of Mystery & The Root: The Association exists for two foundational purposes: to preserve thaumaturgical mystery by concealing it from mundane society (Concealment of Mystery), and to support research aimed at reaching the Swirl of the Root (Akasha).
- Cold Aristocratic Utilitarianism: Humanity, ethics, and emotional bonds are considered utterly irrelevant compared to the advancement of thaumaturgy. Lineage, Magic Crest depth, and academic authority dictate an individual's worth.

[RESOURCES & GLOBAL INFLUENCE]
- Limitless Occult Capital: Centuries of accumulated wealth, global real estate, ownership of Western leylines, private banks, ancient grimoires, and peerless magical artifacts.
- Covert Political Domination: Puppeteers international politicians and law enforcement to quietly alter public records and silence supernatural exposures.

[RELATIONSHIP WITH THE SUPERNATURAL]
- Self-Appointed Masters of Mystery: The Association views all magical phenomena through rigorous Western academic taxonomy. They catalog, codify, and monopolize magecraft, viewing uncontrolled phenomena as threats to their authority.

[INTERNAL CONFLICTS & SECRECY]
- Cutthroat Aristocratic Warfare: Constant political assassination, poisoned tea, sabotage, and bitter ideological battles between aristocratic conservatives (preserving old bloodlines) and democratic reformers.
- Concealment of Mystery: The iron rule punishable by death. Any magus who carelessly reveals magic to modern media is ruthlessly purged.

[RELATIONSHIP WITH JAPAN & FATE TOUCHPOINTS]
- Neglect of the Far East: London views Japan as an exotic, low-priority frontier outside standard Association jurisdiction. They manage it loosely through designated Second Owners (the Tohsaka in Fuyuki).
- Contempt for Indigenous Clans: The Clock Tower views indigenous Japanese demon hunters (Ryougi, Nanaya) as crude, unrefined primitives lacking proper Magic Circuits or thaumaturgical pedigree.
- Crossover Friction: If Clock Tower representatives travel to Mifune, it is solely to track high-value targets (like Touko) or investigate catastrophic breaches of secrecy.

[OUTSIDER KNOWLEDGE & PERCEPTION]
- Mundane World: Completely unaware that the Clock Tower exists.
- Independent Magi: Regard the Clock Tower as a mixture of an academic Mecca and a terrifying, bureaucratic monster that could crush them at any moment.

[ROLEPLAY CONSEQUENCES & SCENE DIRECTION]
- Interacting with Clock Tower agents introduces heavy political paranoia, aristocratic condescension, and pedantic legalism.
- Dialogue is laced with passive-aggressive academic insults, formal English etiquette, and immediate suspicion of any uncataloged supernatural ability.
</Org_Clock_Tower_Mages_Association>

5.content:
<Org_Clock_Tower_Sealing_Designation_Division>
[ORGANIZATIONAL TYPE & IDENTITY]
Occult Specimen Capture & Enforcement Branch (Specialized Division). The lethal executive branch of the Clock Tower (封印指定総括庁) responsible for locating, capturing, and physically preserving magi who have developed singular, irreproducible thaumaturgical miracles.

[STRUCTURE & OPERATIVES]
- Curators & Directors: Bureaucrats in London who evaluate research dossiers and issue official Sealing Designation warrants.
- Enforcers (執行者, Shikkousha): Highly trained, lethal combat specialists contracted by the Association to hunt designated targets. Notable Enforcers include Bazett Fraga McRemitz (Fate), along with brutal occult mercenaries specializing in anti-magus warfare and barrier dismantling.

[IDEOLOGY & METHODS]
- "Preservation Through Containment": A Sealing Designation is technically the Association's "highest honor," but practically a death sentence. The Association does not wish to punish the magus; they wish to preserve their unique thaumaturgical ability for eternity.
- The Formalin Fate: Once captured, the target is vivisected; their brain, nerves, and organs are extracted and preserved in specimen jars in the subterranean archives of London so that future generations can study their flesh.
- Ruthless Hunting Tactics: Enforcers utilize conceptual weapons, ambush tactics, hostage leverage, tracking familiars, and heavy suppression fields. They have zero compunction about collateral damage or eliminating civilian witnesses.

[RESOURCES & EQUIPMENT]
- Unlimited Association Funding: Access to black-market mystic codes, international travel authority, classified intelligence files, and thaumaturgical dampening equipment designed specifically to neutralize magic circuits.

[RELATIONSHIP WITH KARA NO KYOUKAI]
- The Shadow Over Touko: Aozaki Touko received a Sealing Designation for perfecting biological puppetry that creates human replicas indistinguishable from the original soul container. She fled London and lived as a hunted fugitive throughout the 1990s, constantly moving workshops, disguising her presence, and crafting defensive puppets specifically to counter Enforcers.

[INTERNAL CONFLICTS & SECRECY]
- Cutthroat Mercenary Rivalry: Enforcers compete fiercely for the immense bounties attached to Grand-rank designations, sometimes sabotaging fellow agents.
- Absolute Operational Secrecy: Operates in total shadow; even standard Clock Tower students know little of the division beyond the terror of its name.

[INTER-INSTITUTIONAL RELATIONSHIPS]
- Autonomous from standard academic faculties; commands field priority over regular magi.
- Strictly separate from the Holy Church, though Enforcers occasionally cross paths with Church Executors in disputed territories.

[OUTSIDER KNOWLEDGE & PERCEPTION]
- Known to magi as the ultimate boogeyman. The mere mention of a Sealing Designation makes even proud aristocratic magi flee their estates and erase their identities.

[ROLEPLAY CONSEQUENCES & SCENE DIRECTION]
- The arrival of an Enforcer immediately turns any roleplay scene into a high-stakes survival thriller.
- Enforcers do not negotiate, debate philosophy, or accept surrender without containment. Scenes feature cold, efficient tactical breaches, shattered concrete, neutralizing gas, and relentless tracking.
</Org_Clock_Tower_Sealing_Designation_Division>

6.content:
<Org_Holy_Church_and_Executors>
[ORGANIZATIONAL TYPE & IDENTITY]
Militant Heresy-Hunting Division & Relic Custody Agency (Religious Shadow Organization). The covert, martial arm of the Roman Catholic Church (聖堂教会) dedicated to the eradication of heretical entities, demons, vampires (Dead Apostles), and blasphemous violations of Christian doctrine.

[STRUCTURE & RELEVANT BRANCHES]
- Pastoral Papacy: The public, billion-strong Catholic clergy operating global churches and charities, kept entirely ignorant of the occult division.
- Assembly of the Eighth Sacrament (第八秘蹟会): The specialized division charged with the recovery, protection, and management of Holy Relics. Also tasked with supervising anomalous rituals such as the Fuyuki Holy Grail War (e.g., Father Kotomine Risei, Kotomine Kirei).
- The Burial Agency (埋葬機関): The hyper-elite, fanatically lethal pinnacle of demon-killers, operating outside standard Church law.
- Executors (代行者, Daikousha): The frontline combat priests and inquisitors trained in anti-heresy combat, lethal martial arts, and theological purging (e.g., Kotomine Kirei, Caren Hortensia).

[IDEOLOGY & METHODS]
- Total Annihilation of Heresy: While the Mage's Association seeks to study, hoard, and cultivate mystery, the Church seeks to burn, cleanse, and erase anything that contradicts divine dogma. They do not care about the Root; they care about sin, salvation, and demonic corruption.
- Sacramental Combat: Executors utilize scripture-based Baptism Rites (which bypass physical defense to directly disperse spiritual and demonic bodies), enchanted throwing blades (Black Keys), and rigorous physical conditioning (such as Bajiquan).

[RESOURCES & GLOBAL REACH]
- Global Parish Infrastructure: Worldwide surveillance through local parishes, diplomatic immunity via the Holy See, ancient Vatican relic vaults, and extensive mundane political leverage.

[RELATIONSHIP WITH KARA NO KYOUKAI & FATE CROSSOVER]
- Zero Active Jurisdiction in Mifune: During the events of Kara no Kyoukai, the Church has no active missions or administrative presence in Mifune City. Reien Academy operates under a conventional Catholic diocese, completely separated from the militant Eighth Sacrament.
- Crossover Vigilance: In a shared Fate setting, Kotomine Kirei oversees the Fuyuki parish and maintains regional surveillance over surrounding prefectures. If demonic outbreaks or uncontrolled supernatural massacres spill outside Mifune, Church inquisitors would deploy immediately.

[RELATIONSHIPS WITH OTHER INSTITUTIONS]
- Fragile Cold War with the Clock Tower: Regulated by centuries-old non-aggression treaties. They cooperate only under strict ceremonial accords (such as the Holy Grail War supervision) and otherwise view each other with intense ideological hostility.
- Hostility Toward Indigenous Clans: The Church regards indigenous Japanese demon-hunting bloodlines (Ryougi, Nanaya) as unbaptized pagans whose unnatural powers border on heresy.

[OUTSIDER KNOWLEDGE & PERCEPTION]
- Known to ordinary humans only as the peaceful Catholic Church.
- Magi view Church Executors as fanatical, bloodthirsty zealots capable of ignoring basic thaumaturgical logic in their quest to destroy heretics.

[ROLEPLAY CONSEQUENCES & SCENE DIRECTION]
- Encounters with Church agents bring cold theological judgment and immediate tension.
- Executors cannot be reasoned with through academic debate or magical bargains. Their dialogue is quiet, severe, and laden with biblical gravitas, accompanied by the metallic rustle of concealed Black Key hilts and the reciting of Latin verses.
</Org_Holy_Church_and_Executors>

7.name: Org_Four_Demon_Hunter_Houses
key: สี่ตระกูลนักล่าปิศาจ
สี่ตระกูลปราบมาร
7.content:
<Org_Four_Demon_Hunter_Houses>
[ORGANIZATIONAL TYPE & IDENTITY]
Indigenous Japanese Bloodline Alliance (Historical / Defunct Clan Confederation). An ancient feudal coalition of four specialized Japanese clans—Ryougi (両儀), Asagami (浅神), Fujou (巫条), and Nanaya (七夜)—formed centuries ago to hunt, suppress, and exterminate "inhuman" entities (Mixed-Bloods, Oni, and demonic spirits) threatening human settlements.

[STRUCTURE & THE FOUR HOUSES]
- The Ryougi (両儀): Masters of the blade and internal duality; bred heirs with split personas to shoulder the spiritual stain of slaughter. In modern times, adapted into wealthy, reclusive aristocrats in Mifune.
- The Asagami (浅神 / 浅上): Possessors of innate telekinetic/spatial distortion psychic channels. Assimilated into modern corporate construction while attempting to chemically numb and extinguish their psychic bloodline.
- The Fujou (巫条): Specialized in spirit channeling, psychic mediums, and out-of-body astral projection. Completely collapsed by the late 1990s, ending with the tragic, hospitalized Kirie Fujou.
- The Nanaya (七夜): Refined pure human assassin reflexes and superhuman sensory conditioning to slaughter non-humans. Exterminated deep in their mountain redoubt by the Tohno clan, surviving only through Nanaya Shiki.

[IDEOLOGY & METHODS]
- Human Purity Against Monsters: Unlike Western magi who utilize Magic Circuits, incantations, and thaumaturgical foundations, the Four Houses relied entirely on inherited biological mutations, psychic channels, and rigorous mental conditioning to combat monsters as mortal humans.
- Defunct Status: In the late 1990s, the alliance is completely dead. There are no shared meetings, no joint councils, and no mutual assistance. Each family either decayed, integrated into mundane society, or was annihilated.

[RESOURCES & ANCIENT ARTIFACTS]
- Dormant Genetic Pedigree: Unique psychic channels and heightened physical senses passed down through selective breeding.
- Ancestral Armaments: Mastercrafted anti-spirit blades and ceremonial heirlooms (such as Shiki's Bizen Kanesada katana).

[SIGNIFICANCE TO KARA NO KYOUKAI NARRATIVE]
- Araya Souren's Grand Design: Araya Souren recognized that these four houses embodied extreme, unadulterated concepts of human potential. He orchestrated the supernatural incidents in Mifune by manipulating Fujou Kirie (spirit projection), Asagami Fujino (spatial distortion), and Ryougi Shiki (dual container & death perception) to build his conceptual Taiji diagram and open a path to the Root.

[INTER-INSTITUTIONAL RELATIONSHIPS]
- Zero contact with Western Magecraft; historically operated completely outside the Clock Tower's awareness.
- Deep historical animosity toward Oni mixed-bloods and demonic lineages.

[OUTSIDER KNOWLEDGE & PERCEPTION]
- Completely forgotten by modern Japanese society, reduced to obscure local folklore.
- Dismissed by the Clock Tower as primitive Eastern superstition.

[ROLEPLAY CONSEQUENCES & SCENE DIRECTION]
- When Shiki encounters Fujino or learns of Kirie, there is an eerie, melancholy resonance between them—the tragic realization that they are the lonely remnants of an ancient, obsolete warrior caste discarded by the modern world.
- Dialogue referencing the Four Houses carries ancient gravitas, ancestral guilt, and the weight of forgotten bloodlines.
</Org_Four_Demon_Hunter_Houses>

8.content:
<Org_Mifune_Police_and_Underworld>
[ORGANIZATIONAL TYPE & IDENTITY]
Mundane Municipal Law Enforcement & Criminal Syndicate Networks (Civic Infrastructure & Informal Networks). The dual mundane systems responsible for order, legal authority, and organized crime within Mifune City, through which the collateral damage of supernatural violence is absorbed and rationalized.

[STRUCTURE & KEY FIGURES]
- Mifune Police Department (Investigative Division 1 / Homicide): Senior Detective Daisuke Akimi (Mikiya's older cousin). A compassionate, experienced, and observant detective who handles gruesome serial murders, rooftop suicides, and strange urban accidents. He frequently shares confidential case files and autopsy reports with Mikiya over casual diner meals.
- Traditional Yakuza Syndicates: Old-school crime families operating within the sphere of patronage linked to the Ryougi family's aristocratic territory. They control local gambling, hostess bars, and red-light districts with strict territorial discipline, steering clear of Ryougi affairs.
- Street Delinquent & Narcotics Underbelly: Disaffected teenagers, motorcycle gangs, and alleyway drug pushers. The predatory urban fringe that was exploited by Lio Shirazumi to peddle hallucinogenic Blood Chips.

[IDEOLOGY & METHODS]
- Forensic Rationalization: The police investigate crimes through mundane forensics: fingerprints, ballistics, pathology reports, and criminal profiling. They operate strictly under modern civic penal law.
- Underworld Pragmatism: The yakuza prioritize profit, territorial boundaries, and avoiding police crackdowns. They maintain strict codes against unprovoked public violence that attracts official scrutiny.

[RELATIONSHIP WITH THE SUPERNATURAL]
- Complete Cognitive Denial: Mundane authorities are blind to magic and psychic phenomena. When confronted with supernatural slaughter—bodies folded inside out on bridges, corpses drained of blood, or floating apparitions—detectives rationalize the evidence through mundane theories: industrial equipment, experimental chemical weapons, fanatical cult pacts, or psychotic serial killers.

[INTERNAL CONFLICTS & SECRECY]
- Jurisdictional Friction: Tension between local precinct detectives and national investigative bureaus when bizarre, unsolved massacres occur.
- Daisuke's Professional Vulnerability: Daisuke's habit of passing confidential autopsy files and crime scene photos to his civilian cousin Mikiya is an ethical breach that could end his career if discovered.

[INTER-INSTITUTIONAL RELATIONSHIPS]
- Daisuke's unwitting cooperation provides Garan no Dou with essential early-warning intelligence regarding supernatural anomalies.
- Yakuza maintain respectful distance from the Ryougi estate and Shiki's neighborhood.
- Occult agents (Touko, Church fixers) quietly manipulate police reports and bribe officials to maintain the Concealment of Mystery.

[OUTSIDER KNOWLEDGE & PERCEPTION]
- The dominant, visible reality for 99.9% of Mifune's population. Citizens look to police patrols and news broadcasts to understand urban events.

[ROLEPLAY CONSEQUENCES & SCENE DIRECTION]
- Grounding anchor for noir detective roleplay. Characters cannot recklessly engage in public combat without sirens wailing, police cordons establishing, and detective interrogations following.
- Mikiya's access to Daisuke allows characters to investigate crime scenes legally, while Shiki and other armed characters must actively evade patrol cars, hide concealed knives, and slip through rain-soaked back alleys.
</Org_Mifune_Police_and_Underworld>

9.content:
<Org_Broader_Magus_Community_and_Heretics>
[ORGANIZATIONAL TYPE & IDENTITY]
Independent Thaumaturgical Subculture & Rogue Scholars (Informal Occult Network). The decentralized, unregulated collective of independent magi, wandering alchemists, academic defectors, and heretical researchers operating across Japan and the international fringe, outside the direct control of the Clock Tower.

[STRUCTURE & REPRESENTATIVE FIGURES]
- Araya Souren: A former Tendai Buddhist monk who studied thaumaturgy at the Clock Tower before abandoning both Buddhism and Western academia. A master bounded-field architect obsessed with recording human death and reaching the Root, operating from the Ogawa Apartments.
- Cornelius Alba: An arrogant, pedantic former professor of the Sorgan School in the Clock Tower's Department of Puppetry. Obsessed with status and bitter inferiority toward Touko, he allied with Araya out of vanity and vengeance.
- Freelance Fixers & Wandering Alchemists: Unaligned spellcasters who sell memory-wiping charms, boundary wards, and cursed talismans to underworld figures or wealthy eccentrics in private urban workshops.

[IDEOLOGY & METHODS]
- Unrestrained Monomania: Unlike Clock Tower faculty who are constrained by departmental peer review and political decorum, independent heretics pursue their personal thaumaturgical obsessions without ethical boundaries. They treat human lives, urban buildings, and social laws as disposable raw materials.
- Radical Synthesis: Combining Western thaumaturgical foundations with Eastern esoteric traditions, Buddhist cosmology, or psychic experimentation (e.g., Araya's Taiji architecture and Sarira relics).

[RESOURCES & WORKSHOPS]
- Secluded Thaumaturgical Lairs: Abandoned industrial warehouses, condemned skyscrapers, or custom-built residential complexes (like the Ogawa Apartments, designed as a living mandala and magical centrifuge).
- Ancient Relics & Grimoires: Relics plundered from temples or purchased through black-market auctions, outside Association taxation.

[RELATIONSHIP WITH THE SUPERNATURAL WORLD]
- Extreme Heresy & Vulnerability: They operate in perpetual danger from both Clock Tower Enforcers (for Sealing Designations or breaching secrecy) and Holy Church Executors (for heresy and demon manipulation).

[INTERNAL CONFLICTS & SECRECY]
- Treachery & Paranoia: Rogue magi never form true alliances; every partnership is a temporary convenience. Betrayal is standard practice (e.g., Alba attempting to murder Touko, only to be coldly discarded and crushed by Araya).

[RELATIONSHIPS WITH OTHER INSTITUTIONS]
- Hunted or ignored by the Clock Tower; purged on sight by the Holy Church; regarded with intense disdain by indigenous Japanese clans like the Ryougi.

[OUTSIDER KNOWLEDGE & PERCEPTION]
- Totally invisible to mundane humanity until their grand rituals collapse, resulting in unexplained gas explosions, mass suicides, or apartment fires.

[ROLEPLAY CONSEQUENCES & SCENE DIRECTION]
- Provides unpredictable, menacing antagonists for custom roleplay storylines. Rogue magi do not abide by the aristocratic rules of the Holy Grail War or gentlemanly academic codes; they fight dirty, set lethal traps, deploy familiars in civilian crowds, and sacrifice innocents without hesitation.
- Scenes featuring heretical magi evoke the scent of incense burning over rotting floorboards, esoteric Sanskrit diagrams chalked on concrete, flickering fluorescent tubes, and suffocating psychological obsession.
</Org_Broader_Magus_Community_and_Heretics>
